drug_class: Beta-blocker (Non-selective) with Class III antiarrhythmic properties

avoid_supplements.name: Licorice (high dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Licorice causes sodium retention and potassium depletion, increasing QT prolongation risk and hypokalemia which amplifies sotalol's proarrhythmic effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid licorice supplements and high-dose licorice products; monitor serum potassium if licorice exposure occurs

avoid_supplements.name: Hawthorn (high dose)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Hawthorn may potentiate beta-blocker effects and increase risk of bradycardia and hypotension; additive effects on cardiac conduction
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; if patient insists, obtain cardiology clearance and monitor heart rate and blood pressure closely

avoid_supplements.name: Stimulant supplements (Ephedra, synephrine, high-dose caffeine)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Direct antagonism of sotalol's beta-blocking effects; increases risk of tachycardia and loss of antiarrhythmic control
avoid_supplements.action: Strictly avoid all stimulant-containing supplements and limit caffeine intake to <200 mg/day

avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements and high-dose potassium-sparing agents
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Hyperkalemia increases sotalol's potential for QT prolongation and torsades de pointes; renal clearance of both drugs may compete
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid supplemental potassium unless specifically prescribed by cardiologist; monitor serum K+ regularly if concurrent use necessary

caution_supplements.name: Magnesium supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Magnesium deficiency increases QT prolongation risk; supplementation may be protective, but excessive doses could cause GI effects and drug interactions
caution_supplements.action: Monitor serum magnesium levels; supplementation is generally safe at recommended doses (200-400 mg/day) and may be beneficial

caution_supplements.name: Omega-3 fatty acids (fish oil)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Fish oil has mild anticoagulant properties and may potentiate sotalol's bradycardic effects at very high doses; generally considered cardioprotective
caution_supplements.action: Use standard doses (1-3 g/day); monitor for excessive bradycardia or bleeding if on concurrent anticoagulants

caution_supplements.name: CoQ10
caution_supplements.mechanism: CoQ10 may slightly reduce beta-blocker efficacy and has mild antihypertensive effects; potential additive cardioprotective benefit
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate; doses up to 300 mg/day are generally well-tolerated

avoid_foods.name: High sodium processed foods
avoid_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium increases fluid retention and hypertension, potentially counteracting sotalol's antiarrhythmic and blood pressure control benefits
avoid_foods.action: Maintain sodium restriction <2,300 mg/day; target <2 g/day if hypertension or heart failure present

avoid_foods.name: Licorice-containing foods and candies
avoid_foods.mechanism: Licorice causes hypokalemia and sodium retention, increasing QT prolongation and arrhythmia risk
avoid_foods.action: Avoid licorice-containing foods; check labels on candies and herbal teas

caution_foods.name: High potassium foods (bananas, spinach, coconut water, avocado)
caution_foods.mechanism: Normal dietary potassium is generally safe, but excessive intake combined with renal impairment or ACE inhibitors may increase hyperkalemia risk
caution_foods.action: Maintain normal potassium intake; avoid potassium-loading if renal function impaired (eGFR <30) or on concurrent ACE inhibitors/ARBs

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: While sotalol is renally eliminated, grapefruit may have minor effects on renal blood flow and metabolism of concomitant drugs; unlikely to significantly affect sotalol directly
caution_foods.action: No strict prohibition needed, but avoid excessive consumption; monitor for any unexplained changes in heart rate or blood pressure

caution_foods.name: Caffeinated beverages (coffee, tea, energy drinks)
caution_foods.mechanism: Moderate caffeine may slightly antagonize beta-blocker effects; excessive intake increases arrhythmia risk
caution_foods.action: Limit caffeine to <200 mg/day (approximately 2 cups coffee); avoid energy drinks and excessive tea consumption

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, magnesium, and renal function (eGFR) regularly as sotalol is renally cleared and hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia increase QT prolongation and torsades de pointes risk. Baseline and periodic ECG monitoring (QT interval) is essential, particularly if adding supplements or if patient reports palpitations, syncope, or dizziness.
